findings.claim: Order creation is not atomic: if the audit step fails after the order commit, the operation reports failure while leaving an order permanently stored without its required audit record.
evidence: evals/cases/case_01/src/orders.py:17-28 inserts the order, commits it at line 25, and can then raise before inserting the audit record.
evals/cases/case_01/src/orders.py:30-34 performs and commits the audit insert separately, so the two writes do not share one transaction.

Running `pytest -q evals/cases/case_01/tests` produced 1 failed and 1 passed test; test_failed_business_operation_leaves_no_partial_state observed order_count == 1 after the simulated audit failure, although the required atomic result was 0 orders and 0 audit records.
